subject: APAC warm-standby: request for RTO/RPO window & cost-sharing carveout
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Cena <marta.cena@greenline.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 09:15:00 +0000
Subject: APAC warm-standby: request for RTO/RPO window & cost-sharing carveout

Marta —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, GreenLine's requirement for a sub-10m RTO in APAC for the full transaction path would require us to provision a fully hot active stack in the region (dedicated GPUs, pre-warmed KV caches, and synchronous replication for stateful components). That design is feasible, but the incremental monthly cost and long-term commitment are material (~2.6x compared to our standard warm-standby model).

To keep your launch economics reasonable while still improving recovery characteristics, we propose a tailored carveout:

- Payment-critical flows: RTO target 20 minutes, RPO target 1 minute (hot path replicated + prioritized failover).
- Non-critical back-office flows (analytics, batch reconciliation): RTO target 45 minutes, RPO target 1 hour (warm standby with on-demand cache rehydrate).
- Operational guarantees: Traffic steering and automated failover for payment path; controlled manual cutover for analytics with runbook ownership.

Ask: in exchange for relaxing the flat sub-10m commitment for non-critical flows, Redwood will provide a phased pricing adjustment (detailed in the attached cost estimate) and a one-time migration credit covering cross-region pre-warm and failover rehearsals. We can also include a contractual SLA amendment for the split-path RTOs above.

I've attached a draft SLO amendment and a high-level cost spreadsheet. If this sounds workable, can we schedule a 30m session with your SRE and procurement teams next week to go over the numbers and the operating runbook?

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
(karthik.iyer@redwood.ai)

Attachments: slo-amendment-draft.pdf, apac-cost-estimate.xlsx
From: Marta Cena <marta.cena@greenline.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: GreenLine Procurement <procurement@greenline.com>, Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@greenline.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 02:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: APAC warm-standby: request for RTO/RPO window & cost-sharing carveout

Karthik —

Appreciate the quick follow-up and the proposal. A couple of immediate points from our side:

- Payment path: 20m is better than 30–45m, but our ops team is going to push for <=15m for anything that touches payments and dispute handling. We need to see reproducible evidence from a rehearsal (warm failover drill) that your plan meets 20m for at least two consecutive rehearsals before committing.
- Runbook / controls: please include an extract of the failover runbook (who does the DNS cutover, how KV cache replay is handled, rollback steps). Oliver from our SREs will review.
- Procurement angle: our commercial team wants to understand the potential uplift on the committed spend — procurement@greenline.com is on cc and will share target budget ranges.

Can you also share SOC2 / audit evidence for the standby replication paths and any historical MTR for multi-region failovers you have?

Best,
Marta
VP Product Operations — GreenLine Payments

Marta —

Looping in a short technical appendix and an amended SLO draft that addresses the split-path approach. Attached items:

- runbook-extract.txt (high-level steps for payment path failover, DNS cutover timings, KV cache rehydrate strategy)
- slo-amendment-draft.pdf (language for RTO/RPO per flow + credits)
- apac-cost-estimate.xlsx (line-item uplift estimate)

Key clarifications in the appendix:
1) Payment path replication will use near-synchronous replication for transaction state; we reserve an invariant for commit fencing to avoid split-brain. Expected cache rehydrate time (with the proposed pre-warm window) is ~60–90s for the transaction path, which we're factoring into the 20m RTO.
2) For analytics and other batch work, we rely on eventual consistency and snapshot-based rehydration; hence the larger RTO/RPO windows.
3) We propose two rehearsals (non-production) within a 30-day window as an acceptance criteria.

Commercial compromise suggestion: Redwood acknowledges the sensitivity and proposes a 3-month price protection (no uplift over quoted pilot rates) and a 25% service credit for any payment-path failover where RTO > 20m, capped per incident. Full legal redlines to follow if you accept the concept.

Happy to hop on a call with Oliver + procurement — we can bring engineering and SRE to demonstrate the failover playbook.

— Laura
Director, Technical Solutions — Redwood Inference

Karthik / Laura —

We ran the numbers internally and GreenLine is open to proceeding on a 6-month pilot with the split-path SLA approach, subject to:

1) Two successful, observed rehearsals in our staging environment within 45 days.
2) Inclusion of the 25% incident credit for payment-path RTO misses in the SLO amendment.
3) A clear rollback clause and a joint post-rehearsal report template (Oliver will draft).
4) Agreement on the commercial structure: procurement prefers converting the one-time pre-warm into a 6-month amortized monthly addendum.

Please provide a redline-ready SLO amendment and the pilot order form (deal id GL-2026-0987 referenced) and we will loop in our legal. If we can get the paperwork started this week we can target the rehearsals in early November.

Regards,
GreenLine Procurement
